main_text.p: catus,classe quam singulari certamine congredi maluit. Ut & Selymum Imperatorem Turcarum, qui propter exercitus dissensionem, congredi cum frate Amurathe, renuebat.
main_text.head: CAPUT XII.

head.i: Utrum patrem patriæ proditorem liceat occidere?

main_text.p: PRivata Persona publicam devotionemdisf.Clarus in §. Homicidium. vindicat, & quisque in perduellem miles est. Unde à veteribus & modernisnum. 49. Menoch. de Arbitr. judic. quæst. libr 1. quæstio movetur, utrum filius patrem & quidem perduellem licite occidat? Resp. quamvis negativam sententiam plurimi amplectantur & jurisconsulti & casuistæ; eaque forte si secundum affectum loquamur, sit approbanda; sitamen [?] rem rectâ putemus viâ,quæst.90 num.43. Georgius Acacius Enck de Privil.Pa-rent.& liberorum privil.2.0.2.

page.notes: The first line of the top paragraph is continuous from the previous page. The "sitamen" word is broken across lines as "si ta-men" and is marked [?] for the uncertain reading. The notes at the right margin have no reference marks, so each is placed beside the line where it stands. The "dicen-" catchword is at the bottom right. The stray mark at the bottom left and the watermark at the bottom right are not transcribed.
